title: High Throughput Screening with Fluorescent Probe
author: Tjusls China
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6guhbww
materials: Infinite M1000 Pro Automatic Microplate Reader
When the facility ends testing, save data and import it into GraphPad Prism Software. Use “nonlinear fit” – “straight line” to calculate the initial velocity of each reaction a.k.a. its slope value.

steps.title: Clean 96-well plates
steps.instruction: Soak the 96‑well plates in 75 % ethanol, place the container in an ultrasonic cleaner for 30 min to 1 h, wash the plates several times with ddH₂O, then dry them in an oven at 55 °C.

steps.title: Dilute enzyme
steps.instruction: Prepare the enzyme dilution by pipetting 1 µL protein stock into 1 mL buffer and mixing gently; then pipette 200 µL of this protein solution into 12.6 mL buffer to obtain a final concentration of 1.51 nM in the reaction system.

steps.title: Dilute substrate
steps.instruction: Dilute the fluorescent probe CDC‑1 in DMSO to reach a final concentration of 10.2 µM in the reaction system.

steps.title: Dispense protein into wells
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add 94 µL of the prepared protein solution to each well of the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add compounds and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of each FDA‑approved drug library compound to all wells except the first row; add 1 µL 100 % DMSO to the first‑row wells as negative controls; incubate the plate at room temperature for 5 min.

steps.title: Add substrate
steps.instruction: Quickly add 5 µL of the 10.2 µM substrate solution to each well using a multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Configure microplate reader
steps.instruction: Program the Infinite M1000 Pro to shake the plate for 10 s at 654 rpm, then perform kinetic fluorescence measurement for 25 cycles, each cycle lasting 30 s.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Place the plate in the Infinite M1000 Pro reader and start the program to record fluorescence intensity.

steps.title: Calculate activity and inhibition
steps.instruction: For each well, compute residue activity (Ra = Vr / V0 × 100 %) and inhibition ratio (Ir = (1 − Vr / V0) × 100 %); compare compound wells to the negative‑control wells and select compounds with Ra ≈ 80 % for further screening.

steps.title: Repeat screening with selected compounds
steps.instruction: Perform a second screen using only the selected compounds: dispense 94 µL protein into each well, add 1 µL of each chosen compound (with three identical wells as replicates), incubate 5 min at room temperature, add 5 µL substrate, and read fluorescence as in steps 7–8. Collect data and recalculate Ir for higher precision.

steps.title: Perform fluorescence quenching assay
steps.instruction: In a separate plate, mix 94 µL protein with 5 µL substrate and let stand for 30 min; measure the maximum fluorescence (Q1). Then add 1 µL positive compound, measure fluorescence again (Q2), and calculate quenching rate Qr = (Q1 − Q2) / Q1 × 100 %.

steps.title: Identify inhibitors
steps.instruction: Designate compounds as inhibitors if Ir > 80 % and Qr < 20 %; proceed to determine inhibition kinetic constants as needed.
